chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from a man called Sawada, who said:

We were a group in Mina, and the sacrificial animals were too expensive. So we looked around and there was Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) standing upon a flock, bargaining with the sheep, and he was intensively bargaining with them. So we stopped and waited. When he finished, he turned towards us and said: 'I think you have been astounded by my bargaining.' So we said, 'Yes'.

He said: 'The one who is cheated (in excessive spending) is neither praiseworthy nor rewarded. Is there a need for you?' So we said, 'Yes. May Allah keep you well! The sacrificial animals have become too expensive for us.'

He said: 'So gather together and buy a camel among yourselves.' We said, 'And our expenditure would not reach (that).' He said: 'So gather together and buy a cow among yourselves and slaughter it.' We said, 'And our expenditure would not reach (that).'
He said: 'So gather together and buy a sheep among yourselves and slaughter it among yourselves.' We said, 'Does it suffice for seven?' He said, 'Yes, and it suffices for seventy.'

key_terms.الْمَغْبُونُ: The one who is cheated or incurs loss (here, through excessive spending)

ai.seo_question: How many people can one sheep suffice for in Udhiyah (sacrificial offering) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) demonstrates the practical flexibility of *Udhiyah* (sacrificial offering) by advising a group in Mina to pool resources for a single animal when individual costs were prohibitive. He clarifies that the spiritual merit lies in the act of sacrifice rather than excessive expenditure, noting that 'the cheated one is neither praised nor rewarded' for overspending. The Imam further elucidates the jurisprudential ruling that one sheep suffices for seven people, while also indicating the broader capacity for up to seventy, reflecting the Shia scholarly view on the scalability of communal sacrifice.
